spec.name: customers-orders-portal (rep 2)
spec.stack: Next.js (frontend + API) + NestJS + PostgreSQL/Prisma as our usual web stack, with Supabase used ONLY for authentication and file storage. Built locally, NOT deployed.
spec.description: Build a SMALL internal web app, labelled by the owner as 'rep 2', that lists our customers and their orders for internal staff use. Use our USUAL web stack (Next.js + NestJS + PostgreSQL/Prisma) for the application and data layer. However, authentication and file storage MUST be implemented on Supabase — a platform we have NOT used before — scoped to exactly those two concerns (Supabase Auth for login/sessions, Supabase Storage for files); the customers/orders data itself stays in our usual stack DB, not in Supabase. The app is INTERNAL (staff-only, behind Supabase auth). DO NOT DEPLOY it yet — build and verify locally only; no VM sync, no DevOps, no production release. Work entirely inside the project's own folder (default localPath: workspace/projects/customers-orders-portal; create it and build everything there — never at the Odin repo root). ASSUMPTION (state for confirmation): customers/orders are seeded into the local Postgres DB with a small sample dataset for now; if the owner wants real data we can wire customers from HubSpot and orders from Veeqo as a follow-up. Deliver a login screen (Supabase), a customers list, a per-customer orders view, and the ability to attach/view files on a customer or order via Supabase Storage.
features: Supabase authentication: internal staff login/logout with session handling (staff-only access, no public signup)
Per-customer detail showing that customer's orders
Orders listing with key fields (id, date, status, total)
File attachments per customer/order stored in Supabase Storage (upload + view/download)
Local Postgres/Prisma schema + seed data for customers and orders
Local run only (dev server) — no deployment, no VM sync

features.name: Wire real data (HubSpot customers + Veeqo orders)
features.why: We already have HubSpot and Veeqo connected; pulling real customers/orders instead of seed data would make the portal immediately useful — but the brief only said 'lists our customers and their orders', so this is optional until you confirm.

features.name: Role-based access (admin vs viewer)
features.why: Supabase Auth makes row/role gating easy; useful for an internal tool but not requested — add only if you want tiered access.

members.name: Security
members.why: Auth + file storage on a brand-new platform (Supabase) is the main risk area; a Security pass on RLS policies, storage bucket permissions, and session handling would harden it. Not auto-staffed since the brief is small and internal.
